Grok Build TUI

Usage: grok [OPTIONS] [PROMPT] [COMMAND]

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]  Initial prompt for the interactive session

Options:
      --add-dir <DIR>
          Also work in this folder, beside the working directory (repeatable)
      --agent <NAME>
          Agent name or definition file path
      --agents <JSON>
          Inline subagent definitions as JSON
      --allow <RULE>
          Permission allow rule (compat aliases: --allowedTools, --allowed-tools)
      --always-approve
          Auto-approve all tool executions
  -c, --continue
          Continue the most recent session for the current working directory
      --cwd <CWD>
          Working directory
      --debug
          Enable debug logging
      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE
      --deny <RULE>
          Permission deny rule (compat alias: --disallowedTools)
      --disable-web-search
          Disable web search and web fetch tools
      --disallowed-tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to remove (comma-separated)
      --fork-session
          When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original
      --fullscreen
          Open in the standard fullscreen TUI for this session
  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with 'grok help')
      --include-partial-messages
          Emit incremental text and thinking deltas alongside whole messages
      --json-schema <SCHEMA>
          JSON Schema for structured output
      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`
  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model ID to use
      --max-turns <N>
          Maximum number of agent turns
      --minimal
          Experimental: scrollback-native rendering
      --no-alt-screen
          Run inline instead of using the terminal alternate screen
      --no-plan
          Disable plan mode
      --no-subagents
          Disable subagent spawning
      --oauth
          Force browser (loopback) login when the welcome screen authenticates
      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
          Output format for headless mode [default: plain] [possible values: plain, json, streaming-json, streaming-messages-json]
  -p, --single <PROMPT>
          Single-turn prompt. Prints the response to stdout and exits
      --permission-mode <MODE>
          Permission mode [possible values: default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan]
      --prompt-file <PATH>
          Single-turn prompt from a file
      --prompt-json <JSON>
          Single-turn prompt as JSON content blocks
  -r, --resume [<SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>]
          Resume a session by ID or title, or the most recent if omitted
      --reasoning-effort <EFFORT>
          Reasoning effort for reasoning models [aliases: --effort]
      --restore-code
          Restore the original session's repository snapshot when resuming
      --rules <RULES>
          Extra rules to append to the system prompt
  -s, --session-id <SESSION_ID>
          Use a specific session UUID for a new conversation
      --sandbox <PROFILE>
          Sandbox profile for filesystem and network access [env: GROK_SANDBOX=]
      --system-prompt-override <PROMPT>
          Override the agent's system prompt (compat alias: --system-prompt)
      --tools <TOOLS>
          Built-in tools to allow (comma-separated)
  -v, --version
          Print version
      --verbatim
          Send the prompt exactly as given
  -w, --worktree [<WORKTREE>]
          Start the session in a new git worktree, optionally named
      --worktree-ref <WORKTREE_REF>
          Branch, tag, or commit to base the worktree on (with `--worktree`) [aliases: --ref]

Commands:
  agent        Run Grok without the interactive UI
  clone        Lazy-clone a git repository via grove (NFS on macOS, FUSE on Linux)
  completions  Generate shell completion scripts (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, ...)
  dashboard    Open the Agent Dashboard view at startup
  doctor       Check terminal, clipboard, color, and input support without starting Grok
  du           Show what the grok home (~/.grok) uses on disk [aliases: disk-usage]
  export       Export a session transcript as Markdown
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
  inspect      Show the configuration Grok discovers for this directory
  leader       Manage running leader processes
  login        Sign in to Grok
  logout       Sign out and clear cached credentials
  mcp          Manage MCP server configurations
  memory       Manage cross-session memory
  models       List available models and exit
  plugin       Manage plugins and marketplace sources
  sessions     List, search, or restore sessions
  setup        Fetch and install managed configuration
  trace        Export or upload session trace data
  update       Check for updates or install a specific version
  usage        Print persisted token and cost usage for a session
  version      Print version information [aliases: v]
  worker       Run this machine as a Cursor private worker
  worktree     Manage git worktrees
  wrap         Run any command with local clipboard support

      --debug-file <FILE>

In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`

Run a leader in this terminal until Ctrl+C.

The leader registers this machine as a Cursor private worker.

Usage: grok worker start [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Worker display name shown in Cursor.
          
          Default: `[cursor_worker].name`, then the hostname.
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_NAME=]

      --worker-dir <DIR>
          Repository directory offered to Cursor Cloud Agents.
          
          Repeatable (default: `[cursor_worker].worker_dirs`). The first one is the registered working directory.

      --max-agents <N>
          Maximum concurrent Cloud Agent claims.
          
          Default: `[cursor_worker].max_agents`; unset means no cap.

      --pool [<NAME>]
          Join a team Self-Hosted Pool.
          
          Registers a pool worker instead of a personal My Machines worker. One Cloud Agent claims the worker at a time. Needs a team service account credential (`--api-key` or `--auth-token-file`). The pool name defaults to `default`. The worker serves one Cloud Agent run, then stops: when Cursor ends that claim, releases the worker after an hour idle, or offers it a second agent. Claim worktrees stay under the Grok home, so the supervisor must start the next worker on a fresh host or container. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`), as do `--label`, `--labels-file`, `--mint-github-token` and `--sync-dashboard-secrets`.

      --single-use
          Same as `--pool` (legacy alias)

      --pool-name <NAME>
          Deprecated alias for `--pool <NAME>`. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`.
          
          `CURSOR_WORKER_POOL_NAME` names the pool of a bare `--pool` or `--single-use` and is ignored otherwise.

      --mint-github-token
          Let Cursor send the pool worker short-lived GitHub tokens during a claimed run.
          
          Needs `--pool`. A team admin must turn on GitHub token minting for pool workers. Without this flag, the worker refuses the tokens. The worker redacts the token from what the agent sees, best effort.

      --sync-dashboard-secrets
          Let Cursor send the pool worker the team's dashboard secrets as env variables.
          
          They arrive during a claimed run. Needs `--pool`. A team admin must turn on dashboard secret sync for pool workers. The worker redacts them from what the agent sees, best effort.

      --clone-git-repos
          Clone the claimed run's repository with the minted token.
          
          For an any-repo pool worker: a named `--pool` other than `default`, a `--worker-dir` that is not a git checkout with an origin, and no `repo=` or `name=` label. Clones go under the worker's own directory in the Grok home, never into the worker dir; a clone of the same repository there is reused and fetched. Implies `--mint-github-token`.

      --label <KEY=VALUE>
          Routing label for the worker, as `key=value`. Repeatable

      --labels-file <PATH>
          JSON or TOML file of worker labels. Cannot be combined with `--label`
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_LABELS_FILE=]

      --api-key <KEY>
          Cursor API key the worker registers with, in place of your linked Cursor account.
          
          Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`), as does `--auth-token-file`. Prefer `CURSOR_API_KEY`: other local users can read a key passed here in the process list.
          
          [env: CURSOR_API_KEY]

      --auth-token-file <PATH>
          File holding the worker's Cursor auth token, re-read before every reconnect.
          
          The file holds only the token; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Takes precedence over `--api-key`.

      --on-session-start <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim lands. Needs `--pool`.
          
          Runs with `sh -c` in your home directory and gets the session as JSON on stdin. `CURSOR_WORKER_BC_ID` names the agent run. A JSON reply with an `env` object sets variables for the `--on-session-end` command. Stopped after 60 seconds; a failure is logged and never holds up the claim.

      --on-session-end <COMMAND>
          Command run on this host once a pool claim is released. Needs `--pool`.
          
          Runs with `sh -c` in your home directory, after `--on-session-start` finishes, and gets the session and its end `reason` as JSON on stdin. The worker recycles after it finishes, or after 60 seconds; stopping the worker gives it only 5 seconds. A failure is logged and never holds up the teardown.

      --identity-socket
          Give each Cloud Agent its own OIDC identity socket.
          
          Its shells get the path as `CURSOR_AGENT_SOCKET`. An agent POSTs to `/v1/tokens/oidc` on it to mint a short-lived Cursor cloud-agent identity token for an audience it names. Off by default; no socket exists without it. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).

      --management-addr <ADDRESS>
          Serve worker health over HTTP for Kubernetes probes.
          
          ADDRESS is `:8080` (every IPv4 address) or `host:8080`. `GET /healthz` answers 200 while the worker runs, and 503 once it has stopped for good (a rejected credential). `GET /readyz` answers 200 when the worker is connected to Cursor, holds no claim and is not shutting down, and 503 otherwise; its JSON body reports each of those. The worker fails to start when it cannot bind ADDRESS. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).

      --idle-release-timeout <SECONDS>
          Seconds a claim may sit idle before Cursor releases it. 0 turns this off.
          
          Defaults to 3600 for a `--pool` worker, which stops once released, and to 0 otherwise. Cursor still releases claims for its other reasons. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).
          
          [env: CURSOR_WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=]

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --debug-file <FILE>
          Write debug logs to FILE

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --leader-socket <PATH>
          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`.
          
          A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine. Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered. In Grok Build unified, PATH is the leader's own socket, and its shared daemon listens beside it at `PATH.daemon`
